about: Route-choice vectors shared by every platform's RoutePlanner (docs/PLATFORMS.md section 2.2). 'media' is a MediaInfo in FFmpeg vocabulary, 'capabilities' a HardwareCapabilities snapshot in the format a device report prints, 'verdicts' (optional) the decode verdict per video stream index that overrides the snapshot's answer. A rule change edits the contract and its vector in one commit. Device snapshots are provisional: they hold the platform plan's verified facts and list what is assumed or unknown; a real device report replaces them.

vectors.note: Rule 1 needs neither a video nor an audio stream.
The Android probe leaves the pixel format empty; the profile and bit depth still decide.
Rule 2 comes before rule 3: the decoder cannot do it, so the display never matters.
A verdict the caller measured wins over the snapshot.
Refinement of rule 3 (same reason code): the display lists HDR but not the stream's format; never show a wrong picture.
An HDR10+ display also shows HDR10.
Media3 1.11.1 has no profile 7 fallback; a profile 5 decoder would draw it grey and washed out.
An unstated frame rate counts as within the limit.
Audio is re-encoded, video is copied: the route is still the server.
Media3 1.11.1 reads AVI (AviExtractor); docs/PLATFORMS.md [M1] says it does not and is corrected with this file.
Android cannot repackage before stage 5, so the reason stays and the route is the server.
E-AC-3 JOC passthrough works on this box (docs/PLATFORMS.md).
The snapshot lists hardware decoders only; the real report adds the software ones and may turn this into software-decode-too-heavy.
No profile 7 decoder on this box (docs/PLATFORMS.md) and no engine fallback in Media3 1.11.1.
